request: Analyze GSE102284 for PMID 29562317 (Impaired Mitochondrial Energetics Characterize Poor Early Recovery of Muscle Mass Following Hind Limb Unloading in Old Mice.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.assay: bulk RNA-seq (Illumina HiSeq 2500), soleus, male C57BL/6J

condition: RL (10 d unloading + 3 d reloading with voluntary cage ambulation)

final.sample_inclusion: 36 soleus samples: YC 9, YU 4, YR 4, OC 9, OU 6, OR 4 (GEO); paper does not state RNA-seq n per group
final.primary_estimand: Effect of mechanical (un)loading / physical activity on soleus transcriptome within each age: disuse (UN vs CON) and early recovery after 3 d reloading (RL vs CON); the reloading step (RL vs UN) is the re-ambulation (activity resumption) effect. This is a disuse/reloading model, not an exercise-training intervention.
planned_contrasts: UN vs CON in adult (S2.4.p1, FIG4A)
RL vs CON in adult (S2.4.p1, FIG4A)
UN vs CON in old (S2.4.p1, FIG4A)
RL vs CON in old (S2.4.p1, FIG4A)
final.repeated_measure_unit: none; one soleus per independent mouse
final.normalization: Partek Genomics Suite 6.6 quantification on RefSeq transcripts (GEO data_processing)
final.paper_method: R package DESeq (original DESeq, not DESeq2) per GEO data_processing; supplementary methods (S1.8.p1) not available
final.paper_results: No DEG counts reported. KEGG (DAVID) oxidative phosphorylation, TCA cycle and fatty-acid pathways down with UN in both ages and further down with RL (FIG4A, S2.4.p1); Ppargc1a, Esrra, Esrrg mRNA decreased with UN and did not recover (qPCR, FIG4C); transcriptomic response similar in adult and old (S2.4.p2).

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Paper (S1.1.p1, S2.4.p1) defines six groups age x {CON, UN, RL}; FIG4A/B compare UN and RL with control in each age. GEO data_processing names DESeq. The only threshold given for the RNA-seq data is FIG4B legend 'RPKM > 1, p < 0.05' (raw p, no FC). No exercise-training arm exists; the activity manipulation is disuse and reloading (S2.1.p1 '3 days of reloading and voluntary cage ambulation'), which is what the paper intends to study, so it is analysed with that label rather than called exercise.

checks: GEO contact Paul M Coen = paper funding PI (S5.p1)
soleus, male C57BL/6J, 6 and 22-24 mo, UN/RL/CON as in S1.1.p1

ownership.reasoning: Accession cited in the paper; metadata groups match the paper's design.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns are OC_1..YU_4 (age letter, group letter C/U/R, mouse number) with '(Reads)' and '(RPKM)' duplicates; keep the Reads columns and strip the suffix. The metadata key is derived from title ('Young (Adult) Mouse Number 1 in Control Group' -> Y_C_1, normalized to yc1 = YC_1). Age and condition come from the sample group characteristic.

matrix.reasoning: '(Reads)' columns are Partek E/M read assignments to RefSeq transcripts: ~52% integers, fractional values from multi-isoform reads, library sums ~1.7-1.9 M reads; separate RPKM columns are also deposited. Paper input to DESeq was read counts. Summed to gene symbol (Gene column) so the counts are per gene; summing estimated counts is valid. Rounded for DESeq2.

final.analysis_type: factorial (2 ages x 3 conditions), simple effects of condition within age from one model

design.reasoning: Paper compares UN and RL with CON within each age (FIG4A). Reloading vs unloading (activity resumption) and age contrasts/interactions are exploratory. Pooling ages would mix the age factor the paper keeps separate. All males (S1.1.p1).

covariance.reasoning: Independent mice, one sample each; no batch, lane or date recorded in GEO. Age is a design factor, not a covariate.

final.method: DESeq2 (pydeseq2 Wald, joint model on all 36 samples)

paper_route.reason: original DESeq is deprecated/not available in this environment; per-comparison fitting details are in an unavailable supplement

deviations: paper's RPKM > 1 filter approximated by CPM >= 1 in >= 4 samples on the read counts

method.reasoning: Estimated counts support DESeq2, the maintained successor of the paper's DESeq.

final.deviation_note: Paper rule (raw p < 0.05, FIG4B) applied on the DESeq2 route; BH FDR < 0.05 reported as audit.

threshold.reasoning: FIG4 legend B: 'filtered with RPKM > 1, p < 0.05'. No FC cutoff stated.

caveats: No exercise-training arm: the activity manipulation is hind limb unloading (disuse) and 3 d reloading with voluntary cage ambulation; results describe disuse/reloading, not exercise.
Paper reports no DEG counts; comparison is limited to pathway direction and Ppargc1a/Esrra/Esrrg.
Unequal small groups (n = 4 for YU, YR, OR).

study.reasoning: Paper's own route (DESeq) is blocked; DESeq2 runs as a declared deviation with the paper's threshold.

discrepancies.paper: disuse (unloading) and reloading recovery; no exercise training

executions.name: joint
executions.reasoning: One DESeq2 model on all six cells; planned within-age contrasts vs control, plus exploratory reloading-vs-unloading.
